chapter: Cab Calloway's band, Hadacol and closing reflections
title: Hadacol sold for four million dollars and the sugar vats
summary: Danny read in Billboard that Hadacol was sold, then that the buyers found Black workers stirring castor oil and salts by hand in sugar vats.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Yeah. We never got an answer. One of them big combines bought the Hadicol Company for four million dollars. I looked in the Billboard, and it said Senator LeBeau sells the Hadicol Company for four million dollars to Bausch-Lomb or one of them big, famous medicine concerns, conglomerates. Okay.

I'm getting the Billboard, because I'm checking on what's happening with the Hadicol. The next couple of weeks I looked in the Billboard, and there's Senator LeBeau sued by the companies, because they went down there to the plant in Lafayette to see how he was mixing it and what they had. They bought it sight unseen, they was so excited over the thing. Figured they had a (?), see. They went down there, and Senator LeBeau was there -- it was a fiasco, the paper said. When they got down there, Senator LeBeau had got them great big pots they make sugar in...

Vats. There's a big old what looked like a pot, you'd see them on some people's lawns. They used to make sugar cane; you know, granulate sugar. That's what he'd got. He'd got poor/four(?) Black people, men and women there, mixing castor oil, Alka-Seltzer, or salts and sugar, and it's a jive patent medicine -- juniper berries or something in there. And they're stirring it by hand and

they're bottling it by hand. He hasn't got no big plant where you automate, the production line. There's just some Colored people there putting this stuff in the bottles. He had his labels they put on.
And it was a big name, but it wasn't... I mean, the plant was nothin'. You know, like you would expect to see like... Like, with Coca-Cola you'd go in and see them bottling. None of of that.
